c_desc: You want to be a doctor

Medicine is a vast field focused on the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of diseases and disorders in humans. It encompasses various specialties such as internal medicine, surgery, pediatrics, psychiatry, obstetrics and gynecology, and many others.

Dentistry Overview: Dentistry is a branch of healthcare focused on the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of conditions affecting the teeth, gums, and oral cavity. Dentists play a crucial role in maintaining oral health, preventing dental diseases, and restoring smiles.

Veterinary medicine is a profession dedicated to the health and well-being of animals. Veterinarians play a crucial role in ensuring the health of animals, from pets and livestock to wildlife and zoo animals.

Chinese medicine, also known as Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM), is a holistic system of healthcare that has been practiced for thousands of years in China and other parts of Asia. It encompasses various modalities aimed at restoring balance and harmony within the body to promote health and prevent illness.

Optometry is a specialized healthcare profession focused on the eyes and vision care. Optometrists are primary healthcare providers who examine, diagnose, and treat various eye conditions and vision problems.

Pharmacy is a healthcare profession focused on the safe and effective use of medications to improve patients' health outcomes. Pharmacists play a crucial role in various settings, including community pharmacies, hospitals, clinics, and pharmaceutical industries.

Nursing is a noble and essential profession focused on providing compassionate care, promoting health, and supporting individuals, families, and communities across the lifespan. Nurses work in various healthcare settings, including hospitals, clinics, long-term care facilities, community health centers, and home care.

Physiotherapy, also known as physical therapy, is a healthcare profession focused on optimizing physical function, mobility, and quality of life through exercise, manual therapy, and other therapeutic interventions. Physiotherapists work with people of all ages who have injuries, illnesses, or disabilities to help them regain movement and function, manage pain, and prevent further injury.
You want to be a doctor
You want to be a chemical engineer

Nutrition is the science of how food and nutrients affect human health and well-being. It encompasses the study of dietary patterns, nutrient metabolism, food composition, and the relationship between diet and health outcomes.

Biomedical science is a multidisciplinary field that combines aspects of biology, chemistry, physics, and engineering to understand the functioning of the human body and develop solutions to improve human health. Biomedical scientists play a crucial role in research, development, and innovation in areas such as medicine, healthcare, pharmaceuticals, and biotechnology.

Biotechnology is a multidisciplinary field that applies biological principles, techniques, and organisms to develop products and technologies to improve human health, agriculture, and the environment. Biotechnologists work in various industries, including pharmaceuticals, healthcare, agriculture, food production, and environmental science.

Food science is an exciting field that combines scientific principles with the study of food to ensure that the food we eat is safe, nutritious, and delicious. Food scientists play a vital role in every aspect of the food industry, from developing new products to ensuring food safety and quality.

Sport science is a field that combines scientific principles with the study of human movement, exercise physiology, biomechanics, and psychology to enhance athletic performance, prevent injuries, and promote physical activity and well-being.

Marine science is the study of the ocean and its ecosystems, including marine life, oceanography, marine geology, and marine chemistry. It involves exploring the diverse habitats and organisms that inhabit the world's oceans and understanding the interactions between marine organisms and their environment.

Geology is the study of the Earth, its materials, processes, and history. It encompasses the study of rocks, minerals, fossils, landforms, and natural resources, providing insights into the formation of the Earth's crust, geological hazards, and environmental changes over time.

Environmental science is the study of the interactions between humans and the environment, focusing on the impact of human activities on ecosystems, natural resources, and the Earth's systems. It encompasses various disciplines such as ecology, biology, chemistry, geology, and sociology to understand environmental issues and develop sustainable solutions.
You want to be an Engineer

Civil engineering is a branch of engineering that deals with the design, construction, and maintenance of infrastructure and public works. It encompasses various disciplines such as structural engineering, transportation engineering, geotechnical engineering, and environmental engineering to create safe, efficient, and sustainable infrastructure for communities.

Mechanical engineering is a diverse and multidisciplinary field of engineering that applies principles of physics, mathematics, and materials science to design, analyze, and manufacture mechanical systems and devices. Mechanical engineers work on a wide range of projects, from developing innovative technologies to improving existing systems, with applications in industries such as automotive, aerospace, manufacturing, energy, and robotics.

Electrical and electronic engineering is a dynamic field that focuses on the study, design, and application of electrical systems, electronics, and electromagnetism. It encompasses a wide range of technologies, from power generation and distribution to telecommunications, computer systems, and semiconductor devices. Electrical and electronic engineers play a crucial role in developing innovative solutions to address societal needs and advance technology across various industries.

Mechatronic engineering is an interdisciplinary field that integrates principles of mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, and computer science to design and develop intelligent systems and machines. Mechatronic engineers combine expertise in mechanics, electronics, control systems, and computer programming to create innovative solutions for a wide range of applications, including robotics, automation, manufacturing, automotive systems, and consumer electronics.

Chemical engineering is a branch of engineering that applies principles of chemistry, physics, mathematics, and biology to design, manufacture, and operate processes that transform raw materials into valuable products. Chemical engineers work in various industries, including petroleum refining, pharmaceuticals, food and beverage, biotechnology, environmental protection, and materials science.

Aerospace engineering is a specialized branch of engineering that focuses on the design, development, testing, and production of aircraft, spacecraft, satellites, and related systems. Aerospace engineers work on a wide range of projects, from designing commercial airplanes and military aircraft to developing rockets, satellites, and space exploration vehicles.

Petroleum engineering is a specialized branch of engineering that focuses on the exploration, production, and extraction of oil and natural gas resources from underground reservoirs. Petroleum engineers play a crucial role in the petroleum industry, from discovering new oil and gas reserves to optimizing production techniques and ensuring the efficient recovery of hydrocarbon resources.

Environmental engineering is a branch of engineering that focuses on the protection and preservation of the environment and public health. Environmental engineers apply principles of engineering, biology, chemistry, and environmental science to design, implement, and manage solutions for air and water pollution control, waste management, environmental remediation, and sustainable development.
You want to be a teacher

Counseling is a professional practice that involves helping individuals overcome personal challenges, develop coping skills, and improve their mental health and well-being. Counselors provide support, guidance, and interventions to clients dealing with various issues, including mental health disorders, relationship problems, career concerns, and academic difficulties. Counseling encompasses a range of approaches and specialties, including mental health counseling, career counseling, school counseling, marriage and family therapy, and substance abuse counseling.

Psychology is the scientific study of the mind, behavior, and mental processes. It encompasses various subfields, including clinical psychology, counseling psychology, educational psychology, industrial-organizational psychology, and research psychology. Psychologists apply principles of psychology to understand human behavior, emotions, cognition, and development, and to promote mental health, well-being, and social change.

International Relations (IR) is a multidisciplinary field of study that focuses on the interactions between countries, international organizations, and non-state actors in the global arena. Students of International Relations study political, economic, social, and cultural dynamics at the international level, as well as theories and frameworks for understanding international cooperation, conflict, and diplomacy.

A degree in English encompasses the study of English language, literature, linguistics, and communication. Students of English develop strong analytical, critical thinking, and communication skills, as well as a deep understanding of literature, language structures, and cultural contexts. English graduates are well-equipped for a wide range of careers that require effective communication, research, writing, and critical analysis skills.

A degree in Education prepares individuals for careers in teaching, educational administration, curriculum development, counseling, and other roles in the field of education. Education programs typically cover topics such as educational psychology, teaching methodologies, curriculum design, classroom management, assessment, and educational policy. Graduates of Education programs are equipped with the knowledge and skills to work in various educational settings, including schools, colleges, universities, and educational organizations.

A degree in Chinese Studies involves the study of Chinese language, literature, history, culture, and society. Students of Chinese Studies develop proficiency in the Chinese language (Mandarin or other Chinese dialects), as well as a deep understanding of Chinese literature, history, philosophy, and contemporary issues. Chinese Studies programs often offer courses in language acquisition, literature analysis, cultural studies, and interdisciplinary topics related to China and Chinese-speaking communities worldwide.

A degree in Special Education focuses on preparing educators to work with individuals with diverse learning needs, including those with disabilities, learning difficulties, developmental delays, or other special needs. Special education programs emphasize understanding the unique needs and abilities of students, designing individualized education plans (IEPs), implementing specialized teaching strategies, and collaborating with families, educators, and support professionals to promote student learning and development.

A degree in Early Childhood Education prepares individuals to work with young children, typically from birth to eight years old, in various educational settings. Early childhood education programs focus on child development, curriculum design, teaching strategies, and assessment methods tailored to the unique needs and characteristics of young learners. Graduates of Early Childhood Education programs are equipped with the knowledge and skills to promote children's physical, cognitive, social, and emotional development through play-based learning, exploration, and positive interactions.
You want to be a Software Developer

Computer Science is a field of study that focuses on the theory, design, development, and application of computer systems and software. Students of Computer Science learn about algorithms, data structures, programming languages, software engineering, computer networks, artificial intelligence, and other areas related to computing. Computer Science graduates possess strong problem-solving skills, analytical thinking, and programming proficiency, making them valuable in various industries that rely on technology and innovation.

Information Technology (IT) is a broad field that encompasses the use of technology to store, retrieve, transmit, and manipulate data for various purposes. Students of Information Technology learn about computer systems, networks, databases, programming languages, cybersecurity, and other aspects of technology infrastructure and applications. IT professionals play a critical role in designing, implementing, and managing information systems that support the operations and objectives of organizations across different industries.

Software Engineering is a specialized field within computer science that focuses on the design, development, testing, and maintenance of software systems and applications. Students of Software Engineering learn about software development methodologies, programming languages, software architecture, algorithm design, and quality assurance techniques. Software engineers are responsible for creating reliable, efficient, and scalable software solutions that meet the needs of users and organizations.

Cybersecurity is a rapidly growing field focused on protecting computer systems, networks, and data from cyber threats, attacks, and breaches. Students of Cybersecurity learn about information security principles, cryptography, network security, ethical hacking, digital forensics, and risk management. Cybersecurity professionals play a crucial role in safeguarding digital assets, ensuring privacy and confidentiality, and maintaining the integrity and availability of information in an increasingly interconnected and digital world.

Cloud Computing is a technology that enables the delivery of computing services, such as servers, storage, databases, networking, software, and analytics, over the Internet (the cloud). Students of Cloud Computing learn about cloud architecture, virtualization, distributed computing, cloud security, and cloud service models, such as Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS), Platform as a Service (PaaS), and Software as a Service (SaaS). Cloud Computing professionals play a crucial role in designing, implementing, and managing cloud-based solutions that provide scalability, flexibility, and cost-effectiveness to organizations across different industries.

Mobile Technology encompasses the development and implementation of applications, systems, and solutions for mobile devices, such as smartphones, tablets, wearables, and Internet of Things (IoT) devices. Students of Mobile Technology learn about mobile app development, mobile operating systems, user interface design, mobile security, and emerging technologies in the mobile space. Mobile Technology professionals play a crucial role in creating innovative mobile applications and services that enhance user experiences and drive digital transformation across various industries.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) is a rapidly growing field of computer science focused on creating intelligent systems that can perform tasks that typically require human intelligence. Students of Artificial Intelligence learn about machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, computer vision, robotics, and other AI techniques and applications. AI professionals develop algorithms, models, and systems that can analyze data, recognize patterns, make decisions, and interact with the environment autonomously or semi-autonomously.

Multimedia Technology is a field that combines various forms of media, such as text, graphics, audio, video, and animation, to create interactive and engaging content for different platforms and purposes. Students of Multimedia Technology learn about digital media production, multimedia design, web development, animation, video editing, and interactive media. They develop skills in visual communication, storytelling, and technical proficiency with multimedia tools and technologies.

Data Science & Analytics is an interdisciplinary field that combines statistics, mathematics, computer science, and domain knowledge to extract insights and value from data. Students of Data Science & Analytics learn about data collection, data preprocessing, data analysis, machine learning, data visualization, and big data technologies. They develop skills in data mining, predictive modeling, and data-driven decision-making to solve complex problems and drive business outcomes across various industries.
You want to be an Architect

Architecture is the art and science of designing and planning buildings, structures, and spaces that are both functional and aesthetically pleasing. Students of Architecture learn about architectural history, theory, design principles, building technology, sustainability, and construction methods. They develop skills in architectural drafting, computer-aided design (CAD), model making, and project management to create innovative and sustainable architectural solutions that meet the needs of users and communities.

Quantity Surveying is a profession that involves the management and control of construction costs and contracts throughout the entire construction process, from inception to completion. Students of Quantity Surveying learn about construction economics, cost estimation, contract administration, project management, and construction law. They develop skills in cost analysis, procurement, financial management, and dispute resolution to ensure that construction projects are delivered on time, within budget, and to the required quality standards.

Real Estate Management is a discipline that involves the administration, operation, and investment management of real estate properties. Students of Real Estate Management learn about real estate principles, property valuation, investment analysis, property law, and real estate finance. They develop skills in property management, leasing, asset valuation, market research, and portfolio management to maximize the value and performance of real estate assets for property owners, investors, and developers.
You want to be a Public Speaker

Advertising is a field within marketing that involves creating and delivering persuasive messages to target audiences to promote products, services, or ideas. Students of Advertising learn about advertising principles, consumer behavior, branding, communication strategies, creative development, and media planning. They develop skills in copywriting, graphic design, market research, campaign management, and digital marketing to create impactful advertising campaigns that resonate with consumers and achieve marketing objectives.

Broadcasting is a field within the media industry that involves the production and distribution of audio and visual content through various platforms, such as radio, television, and online streaming services. Students of Broadcasting learn about media production techniques, storytelling, journalism ethics, broadcast technology, and audience engagement strategies. They develop skills in scriptwriting, video production, audio editing, broadcasting equipment operation, and content distribution to create compelling and informative media content for diverse audiences.

Journalism is the practice of gathering, analyzing, and disseminating news and information to the public through various media platforms, such as print, broadcast, and digital media. Students of Journalism learn about journalistic ethics, news writing, investigative reporting, media law, and multimedia storytelling techniques. They develop skills in research, interviewing, writing, editing, and multimedia production to produce accurate, objective, and engaging news content that informs and educates audiences.

Public Relations (PR) is a strategic communication discipline that involves managing and maintaining positive relationships between organizations, individuals, and the public. Students of Public Relations learn about communication theory, media relations, crisis management, brand reputation, stakeholder engagement, and strategic planning. They develop skills in writing, public speaking, event management, social media management, and relationship building to create and execute PR campaigns that enhance brand image, reputation, and credibility.

Law is a field that encompasses the study of legal principles, systems, and institutions, as well as the application of those principles to resolve disputes, uphold justice, and regulate society. Students of Law learn about various branches of law, such as criminal law, civil law, constitutional law, and commercial law. They develop skills in legal research, analysis, advocacy, negotiation, and problem-solving to pursue careers in legal practice, academia, government, business, or non-profit organizations.
You want to be a Business Man

Actuarial Science is a discipline that involves the application of mathematical and statistical methods to assess and manage financial risks in various industries, such as insurance, finance, and investment. Students of Actuarial Science learn about probability theory, mathematical modeling, financial mathematics, and risk management techniques. They develop skills in data analysis, predictive modeling, and actuarial software to analyze and quantify risks, and to design and price insurance products, pension plans, and investment strategies.

Accounting is a discipline that involves the measurement, processing, and communication of financial information about economic entities, such as businesses, governments, and non-profit organizations. Students of Accounting learn about financial reporting standards, auditing principles, taxation laws, managerial accounting techniques, and business analysis methods. They develop skills in financial accounting, cost accounting, auditing, taxation, and financial analysis to prepare and interpret financial statements, assess business performance, and support decision-making processes.

Finance is a field that involves the management of money, investments, and financial assets to maximize value and achieve financial goals. Students of Finance learn about financial markets, investment analysis, corporate finance, risk management, and financial decision-making. They develop skills in financial analysis, portfolio management, financial modeling, and financial planning to analyze investment opportunities, assess risks, and optimize financial performance for individuals, corporations, and financial institutions.

Economics is a social science discipline that studies how individuals, businesses, governments, and societies allocate resources to meet their needs and achieve their goals. Students of Economics learn about economic theories, principles, and models to analyze and understand various economic phenomena, such as production, consumption, distribution, and market behavior. They develop skills in economic analysis, statistical methods, and policy evaluation to address real-world economic challenges and inform decision-making in government, business, and academia.

Marketing is a dynamic field that involves creating, communicating, delivering, and exchanging offerings that have value for customers, clients, partners, and society at large. Students of Marketing learn about consumer behavior, market research, branding, advertising, digital marketing, and marketing strategy. They develop skills in market analysis, marketing communication, customer relationship management, and product development to identify market opportunities, develop marketing plans, and implement marketing campaigns that drive business growth and profitability.

Logistics is the management of the flow of goods, services, and information between the point of origin and the point of consumption to meet customer requirements efficiently and effectively. Students of Logistics learn about supply chain management, transportation, inventory control, warehousing, procurement, and distribution. They develop skills in logistics planning, operations management, process optimization, and supply chain analytics to ensure the smooth and cost-effective movement of goods and services throughout the supply chain network.

International Business is a field that focuses on the study of business activities that involve cross-border transactions between companies and nations. Students of International Business learn about global trade, international marketing, multinational corporations, cross-cultural management, and international finance. They develop skills in international market analysis, global strategy formulation, foreign market entry, and international business operations to navigate the complexities of the global marketplace and capitalize on international business opportunities.

Business Psychology, is the application of psychological principles and methods to enhance individual and organizational performance and well-being in the workplace. Students of Business Psychology learn about organizational behavior, human resource management, employee motivation, leadership, and organizational development. They develop skills in psychological assessment, performance management, talent development, and workplace interventions to address organizational challenges and improve employee satisfaction, productivity, and engagement.

E-commerce, or electronic commerce, refers to the buying and selling of goods and services over the internet. E-business, or electronic business, encompasses a broader range of online business activities, including online transactions, digital marketing, e-payment systems, supply chain management, and customer relationship management. Students of E-commerce/E-Business learn about online business models, digital marketing strategies, e-commerce platforms, payment gateways, cybersecurity, and legal and regulatory issues in e-commerce. They develop skills in website development, online marketing, data analytics, and e-commerce management to capitalize on the opportunities of the digital economy.

Human Resource Management (HRM) involves managing an organization's most valuable asset: its people. Students of HRM learn about various aspects of managing human resources, including recruitment, selection, training and development, compensation and benefits, employee relations, performance management, and HR strategy. They develop skills in communication, conflict resolution, organizational behavior, and labor law to effectively manage employees and contribute to organizational success.

Business Management/Administration focuses on the principles and practices of managing businesses and organizations effectively. Students of Business Management/Administration learn about various aspects of business operations, including strategic planning, finance, marketing, human resources, operations management, and organizational behavior. They develop skills in leadership, decision-making, problem-solving, communication, and teamwork to lead and manage organizations in today's dynamic business environment.
You want to be a designer

A degree in Fine Art involves the study and creation of visual arts, including painting, drawing, sculpture, printmaking, ceramics, photography, and digital art. Students of Fine Art explore various artistic techniques, styles, and concepts, develop their artistic skills, and cultivate their creative expression. They learn about art history, aesthetics, critical theory, and contemporary art practices to become proficient artists and thinkers in the field of visual arts.

A degree in Illustration focuses on the creation of visual narratives and imagery to convey ideas, messages, and stories across various media platforms. Students of Illustration develop skills in drawing, painting, digital illustration, storytelling, and visual communication. They learn about illustration techniques, art theory, character design, narrative development, and industry-standard software tools to become proficient illustrators capable of working in diverse fields such as publishing, advertising, animation, and digital media.

A degree in Animation focuses on the creation of moving images and visual effects through the use of digital technology, traditional animation techniques, and storytelling principles. Students of Animation learn about animation production pipelines, character design, motion graphics, 3D modeling, rigging, texturing, lighting, rendering, and compositing. They develop skills in animation software such as Autodesk Maya, Adobe After Effects, and Toon Boom Harmony to create animations for various platforms including films, television, video games, web content, and mobile applications.

A degree in Game Design focuses on the creation and development of interactive digital experiences, including video games, mobile games, virtual reality (VR) games, and augmented reality (AR) experiences. Students of Game Design learn about game mechanics, level design, storytelling, game engines, user experience (UX) design, and game production pipelines. They develop skills in game programming, 3D modeling, animation, sound design, game testing, and project management to create compelling and immersive gaming experiences for players.

A degree in Graphic Design focuses on the creation of visual communication materials using typography, imagery, layout, and color. Students of Graphic Design learn about design principles, branding, advertising, digital media, and print production. They develop skills in graphic design software such as Adobe Photoshop, Illustrator, and InDesign to create visual assets for various applications including branding, advertising, editorial design, web design, packaging, and digital marketing.

A degree in Fashion Design focuses on the creation of clothing, accessories, and fashion collections that reflect current trends, cultural influences, and individual creativity. Students of Fashion Design learn about fashion history, garment construction, pattern making, textile selection, fashion illustration, and fashion marketing. They develop skills in design conceptualization, draping, sewing, digital pattern drafting, and fashion presentation to create innovative and marketable fashion designs for various segments of the fashion industry.

A degree in Multimedia Design focuses on the creation of digital content that integrates various forms of media, including graphics, animation, video, sound, and interactive elements. Students of Multimedia Design learn about design principles, digital media technologies, user experience (UX) design, and multimedia production processes. They develop skills in graphic design, motion graphics, video editing, web design, user interface (UI) design, and multimedia storytelling to create engaging and immersive digital experiences for various platforms including websites, mobile applications, social media, and interactive installations.

A degree in Interior Design focuses on the planning, design, and decoration of interior spaces to create functional, aesthetically pleasing, and well-designed environments. Students of Interior Design learn about space planning, architectural elements, furniture design, color theory, lighting design, materials, and building codes. They develop skills in design software, hand drafting, technical drawing, 3D modeling, and presentation techniques to create interior design solutions for residential, commercial, hospitality, healthcare, and institutional spaces.
You want to work in a hotel

A degree in Culinary Arts focuses on the art and science of food preparation, cooking techniques, culinary principles, and kitchen management. Students of Culinary Arts learn about culinary history, gastronomy, nutrition, menu planning, food safety, and sanitation. They develop hands-on culinary skills in knife techniques, cooking methods, flavor profiles, recipe development, and presentation to create delicious and aesthetically pleasing dishes. Culinary Arts programs often include practical kitchen experiences, internships, and industry placements to prepare students for careers in the culinary industry.

A career in bakery involves the art and science of baking a variety of bread, pastries, cakes, and desserts. Bakers create delicious baked goods using a combination of ingredients such as flour, yeast, sugar, eggs, butter, and flavorings. They utilize various baking techniques, equipment, and recipes to produce high-quality baked products that meet customer preferences and dietary needs. Bakers work in different settings including bakeries, patisseries, cafes, restaurants, hotels, supermarkets, and specialty food shops.

A degree in Hotel Management prepares students for careers in the hospitality industry, focusing on the management and operation of hotels, resorts, restaurants, and other lodging establishments. Students learn about various aspects of hotel management, including hotel operations, guest services, food and beverage management, event planning, marketing, human resources, and financial management. Hotel Management programs typically combine theoretical knowledge with practical training, internships, and industry placements to equip students with the skills and expertise needed to succeed in the dynamic and fast-paced hospitality sector.

A degree in Tourism Management focuses on the planning, development, and management of tourism-related activities, destinations, and services. Students learn about various aspects of tourism, including tourism marketing, destination management, hospitality operations, sustainable tourism practices, and travel industry trends. Tourism Management programs typically provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the tourism industry, tourism economics, cultural tourism, ecotourism, and adventure tourism. Practical training, internships, and industry placements are often incorporated into the curriculum to prepare students for careers in the diverse and dynamic field of tourism.

A degree in Event Management focuses on the planning, coordination, and execution of various events, including conferences, meetings, exhibitions, weddings, festivals, concerts, and corporate events. Students learn about event planning principles, event marketing, budgeting, logistics, risk management, and event technology. Event Management programs often incorporate practical training, internships, and hands-on experiences to prepare students for careers in the dynamic and fast-paced field of event management.

A degree in Music offers comprehensive training in music theory, performance, composition, music history, and music technology. Students develop their musical skills and knowledge through a combination of practical instruction, ensemble participation, music theory classes, and academic study. Music degree programs typically offer specializations in areas such as classical music, jazz, contemporary music, music education, composition, music technology, and music therapy. Graduates of Music programs pursue diverse careers in music performance, teaching, composition, production, research, and arts administration.

A degree in Mass Communication focuses on the study of communication theories, media production, journalism, public relations, advertising, digital media, and communication research. Students learn about various forms of mass media, including print, broadcast, digital, and social media, and develop skills in media writing, reporting, editing, multimedia production, strategic communication, and audience analysis. Mass Communication programs prepare students for careers in media, journalism, public relations, advertising, marketing, corporate communication, digital media, and related fields.
